name: Tegoprazan

overview.mechanism: Suppresses gastric acid secretion through potassium-competitive inhibition of the gastric proton pump.
uses: Treatment of erosive esophagitis has been evaluated in randomized trials; confirm the Philippine product’s approved indications.

paragraphs.text: In a randomized, double-blind Korean phase 3 trial of 302 patients with endoscopically confirmed erosive esophagitis, both tegoprazan groups were noninferior to esomeprazole for cumulative healing by eight weeks. Healing was 98.9% in each evaluated group, with comparable reported adverse-event incidence. The trial establishes short-term comparative healing, rather than superiority or long-term safety.

A separate 351-patient randomized study examined maintenance after healing, predominantly in Los Angeles grade A or B disease. Endoscopic remission at 24 weeks was 90.6% with tegoprazan versus 89.5% with lansoprazole, meeting the study’s noninferiority criterion; reported safety profiles were similar.

The maintenance result mainly concerns healed mild esophagitis. It should not be generalized to all severe disease, indefinite treatment, or prevention of gastric cancer. These gastrointestinal trials do not establish a kidney-protective effect or a dosing regimen for advanced CKD and dialysis. Product-specific renal prescribing information is needed.
